problem.summary: 构建通用视觉语言模型面临挑战，因为视觉输入的丰富分布和任务多样性使得模型难以泛化到未见过的任务。尽管视觉语言预训练已被广泛研究，但视觉语言指令调优仍待探索。

motivation.summary: NLP中的指令调优已被证明是创建通用语言模型的有效方法。然而，将指令调优应用于视觉语言任务的研究不足。本文旨在通过系统性的视觉语言指令调优研究，提升模型在多样化视觉语言任务上的零样本泛化能力。

core_idea.summary: 基于预训练的BLIP-2模型，进行视觉语言指令调优。通过收集26个公开数据集并转换为指令格式，并引入指令感知的Query Transformer（Q-Former）来提取针对给定指令的信息性视觉特征，从而提升模型对指令的理解和任务泛化能力。

method.summary: 1. 数据构建：收集26个公开视觉语言数据集，涵盖11个任务类别，转换为指令调优格式。2. 模型架构：基于BLIP-2，使用冻结的图像编码器和LLM，通过指令感知的Q-Former提取视觉特征作为软提示输入LLM。3. 训练策略：采用平衡的数据集采样策略（概率与数据集大小的平方根成正比），并使用语言建模损失进行指令调优。4. 推理方法：对于分类/多选任务，采用词汇排名方法；对于生成任务，直接生成响应。

experiments.summary: 在13个留出数据集上进行零样本评估，与BLIP-2和Flamingo模型对比。同时进行消融研究，验证指令感知视觉特征和平衡数据采样策略的有效性。此外，在特定下游任务上进行微调实验。

claims.claim: InstructBLIP在所有13个留出数据集上实现了新的零样本SOTA性能。
指令感知的视觉特征提取显著提升了模型性能，尤其在涉及空间和时间视觉推理的数据集上。
平衡的数据集采样策略改善了整体性能。
InstructBLIP可作为下游任务微调的更好权重初始化模型。
视觉语言指令调优比多任务学习更能提升零样本泛化能力。

limitations.limitation: 1. 模型依赖于预训练的BLIP-2架构和冻结的LLM，可能限制其进一步优化。2. 指令调优数据集虽多样，但可能仍无法覆盖所有视觉语言任务。3. 对于某些任务（如OKVQA），性能仍低于参数量更大的模型（如PaLM-E）。

nodes.title: 视觉语言指令调优框架
nodes.label: InstructBLIP
nodes.summary: InstructBLIP是一个基于BLIP-2的视觉语言指令调优框架，旨在通过指令调优提升模型在多样化视觉语言任务上的泛化能力。
nodes.description: 该框架通过收集26个公开数据集并转换为指令格式，使用指令感知的Q-Former提取视觉特征，并采用平衡的数据集采样策略进行训练。

nodes.title: 指令感知的Query Transformer
nodes.label: Instruction-aware Q-Former
nodes.summary: 指令感知的Q-Former是InstructBLIP的核心组件，它根据给定的指令提取信息性视觉特征，而不是使用指令无关的静态视觉表示。
nodes.description: Q-Former从冻结的图像编码器的输出嵌入中提取视觉特征，并将指令作为输入的一部分，从而生成针对任务的视觉表示。这些视觉特征作为软提示输入到冻结的LLM中。

nodes.title: 平衡的数据集采样策略
nodes.label: Balanced Dataset Sampling
nodes.summary: 为了解决数据集大小差异导致的过拟合和欠拟合问题，提出了一种平衡的数据集采样策略。
nodes.description: 采样概率与数据集大小的平方根成正比，并手动调整某些数据集的权重以优化训练。该策略改善了整体性能。

nodes.title: 指令调优数据构建
nodes.label: Instruction Tuning Data Construction
nodes.summary: 收集26个公开视觉语言数据集，涵盖11个任务类别，并将其转换为指令调优格式。
nodes.description: 数据集被分为13个留入数据集和13个留出数据集。留入数据集用于训练，留出数据集用于零样本评估。训练时混合所有留入训练集，并均匀采样指令模板。

nodes.title: 训练与评估协议
nodes.label: Training and Evaluation Protocols
nodes.summary: 定义了训练和评估的具体协议，包括数据集划分、训练损失和评估方法。
nodes.description: 训练使用语言建模损失。评估分为留入评估和留出零样本评估。对于分类/多选任务，采用词汇排名方法；对于生成任务，直接生成响应。

nodes.title: 模型架构变体
nodes.label: Model Architecture Variants
nodes.summary: InstructBLIP采用四种BLIP-2变体，使用相同的图像编码器但不同的冻结LLM。
nodes.description: 变体包括FlanT5-XL (3B), FlanT5-XXL (11B), Vicuna-7B和Vicuna-13B。所有模型从预训练的BLIP-2检查点初始化。

edges.description: InstructBLIP框架包含指令感知的Q-Former模块。

deltas.before: BLIP-2使用指令无关的Q-Former提取静态视觉特征，不考虑任务指令。
deltas.after: InstructBLIP引入指令感知的Q-Former，将指令作为输入的一部分，提取针对任务的视觉特征。
deltas.why_it_matters: 指令感知的视觉特征提取使模型能够根据任务指令调整视觉表示，从而提升在多样化任务上的性能，尤其在需要空间或时间推理的任务上。

deltas.before: BLIP-2的训练可能使用简单的数据混合策略，未考虑数据集大小差异。
deltas.after: InstructBLIP采用平衡的数据集采样策略，采样概率与数据集大小的平方根成正比，并手动调整权重。
deltas.why_it_matters: 该策略缓解了因数据集大小差异导致的过拟合和欠拟合问题，改善了整体性能和泛化能力。

deltas.before: BLIP-2主要使用图像描述数据进行训练，任务多样性有限。
deltas.after: InstructBLIP收集26个公开数据集，涵盖11个任务类别，并转换为指令调优格式，进行系统性的视觉语言指令调优。
deltas.why_it_matters: 多样化的指令调优数据使模型能够学习更广泛的视觉语言任务，提升零样本泛化能力。

deltas.before: BLIP-2在零样本评估中表现有限。
deltas.after: InstructBLIP在所有13个留出数据集上实现了新的零样本SOTA性能，显著优于BLIP-2和更大的Flamingo模型。
deltas.why_it_matters: 证明了视觉语言指令调优的有效性，使模型能够更好地泛化到未见过的任务和数据集。

main_result.description: 在13个留出数据集上的零样本评估结果，与BLIP-2和Flamingo模型对比。
main_result.key_findings: InstructBLIP在所有13个留出数据集上实现了新的SOTA性能。例如，InstructBLIP FlanT5-XL在六个共享评估数据集上平均相对改进24.8%，优于Flamingo-80B。

ablation.description: 消融研究，验证指令感知视觉特征和平衡数据采样策略的有效性。
ablation.key_findings: 移除指令感知视觉特征导致性能显著下降，尤其在ScienceQA（↓7.0）和iVQA（↓5.6）上。移除数据平衡策略也导致性能下降，但幅度较小。

scaling.description: 使用不同大小的LLM（3B, 7B, 11B, 13B）进行实验。
scaling.key_findings: InstructBLIP在不同LLM上均表现出一致的改进。例如，InstructBLIP FlanT5-XL (4B参数) 优于 Flamingo-80B。

case_study.description: 定性分析，展示InstructBLIP在复杂视觉推理、知识接地图像描述和多轮对话方面的能力。
case_study.key_findings: InstructBLIP能够进行复杂推理（如从场景推断灾难类型）、连接视觉输入与文本知识（如介绍名画），并自适应调整响应长度。

benchmark.description: 在多个标准视觉语言基准上进行评估，包括GQA、ScienceQA、IconQA、VizWiz、iVQA等。
benchmark.key_findings: InstructBLIP在多个基准上取得SOTA性能。例如，在ScienceQA（图像上下文）上达到90.7%准确率。

efficiency.description: 训练效率：所有模型在16个Nvidia A100 (40G) GPU上训练，1.5天内完成。
efficiency.key_findings: 训练效率较高，但未提供详细的推理时间或计算成本分析。

terms.definition: 使用自然语言指令描述的视觉语言任务数据对模型进行微调，以提升模型遵循指令和泛化到新任务的能力。
InstructBLIP中的核心模块，它接收图像编码器的输出和任务指令作为输入，提取针对该指令的视觉特征，并将其作为软提示输入到LLM中。

terms.term: 平衡的数据集采样策略
terms.definition: 一种训练数据采样方法，其中每个数据集被采样的概率与其大小的平方根成正比，以缓解数据集大小差异带来的不平衡问题。
在指令调优中，留入数据集用于模型训练，留出数据集用于零样本评估，以测试模型的泛化能力。
在推理时，对于分类或多选任务，模型生成答案时限制词汇表为候选列表，并计算每个候选的对数似然，选择最高者作为预测。
一个视觉语言预训练模型，使用Q-Former将冻结的图像编码器与冻结的LLM连接起来。

required_models: 预训练的BLIP-2模型（使用ViT-g/14图像编码器）

steps.description: 1. 准备数据集：收集26个公开数据集，并按照论文描述转换为指令调优格式。
2. 准备模型：下载预训练的BLIP-2检查点和对应的冻结LLM。
3. 实现指令感知的Q-Former：修改BLIP-2的Q-Former，使其能够接收指令作为输入。
4. 实现平衡的数据集采样策略：根据数据集大小的平方根计算采样概率，并手动调整某些数据集的权重。
5. 训练：使用语言建模损失，在混合的留入数据集上进行指令调优，最多60K步。
6. 评估：在留出数据集上进行零样本评估，对于分类/多选任务使用词汇排名方法。

metadata.title: InstructBLIP: Towards General-purpose Vision-Language Models with Instruction Tuning
metadata.paper_type: Computer Vision / Pose Estimation / Vision-Language / Vision-Language / Multimodal / Computer Vision / Transformer / Computer Vision / Top-cited Computer Vision paper
metadata.abstract: Large-scale pre-training and instruction tuning have been successful at creating general-purpose language models with broad competence. However, building general-purpose vision-language models is challenging due to the rich input distributions and task diversity resulting from the additional visual input. Although vision-language pretraining has been widely studied, vision-language instruction tuning remains under-explored. In this paper, we conduct a systematic and comprehensive study on vision-language instruction tuning based on the pretrained BLIP-2 models. We gather 26 publicly available datasets, covering a wide variety of tasks and capabilities, and transform them into instruction tuning format. Additionally, we introduce an instruction-aware Query Transformer, which extracts informative features tailored to the given instruction. Trained on 13 held-in datasets, InstructBLIP attains state-of-the-art zero-shot performance across all 13 held-out datasets, substantially outperforming BLIP-2 and larger Flamingo models. Our models also lead to state-of-the-art performance when finetuned on individual downstream tasks (e.g., 90.7% accuracy on ScienceQA questions with image contexts). Furthermore, we qualitatively demonstrate the advantages of InstructBLIP over concurrent multimodal models. All InstructBLIP models are open-sourced at https://github.com/salesforce/LAVIS/tree/main/projects/instructblip.

1 Introduction
A longstanding aspiration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) research is to build a single model that can solve arbitrary tasks specified by the user. In natural language processing (NLP), instruction
tuning [46, 7] proves to be a promising approach toward that goal. By finetuning a large language

model (LLM) on a wide range of tasks described by natural language instructions, instruction tuning enables the model to follow arbitrary instructions. Recently, instruction-tuned LLMs have also been leveraged for vision-language tasks. For example, BLIP-2 [20] effectively adapts frozen instruction-
tuned LLMs to understand visual inputs and exhibits preliminary capabilities to follow instructions in

image-to-text generation. Compared to NLP tasks, vision-language tasks are more diverse in nature due to the additional visual inputs from various domains. This poses a greater challenge to a unified model that is supposed to generalize to diverse vision-language tasks, many unseen during training. Most previous work can be grouped into two approaches. The first approach, multitask learning [6, 27], formulates various vision-language tasks into the same input-output format. 2 Vision-Language Instruction Tuning

InstructBLIP aims to address the unique challenges in vision-language instruction tuning and provide a systematic study on the models’ improved generalization ability to unseen data and tasks. In this section, we first introduce the construction of instruction-tuning data, followed by the training and evaluation protocols. Next, we delineate two techniques to improve instruction-tuning performance from the model and data perspectives, respectively. Lastly, we present the implementation details.
2.1 Tasks and Datasets

2.2 Training and Evaluation Protocols

To ensure sufficient data and tasks for training and zero-shot evaluation, we divide the 26 datasets into 13 held-in datasets and 13 held-out datasets, indicated by yellow and white respectively in Figure 2. We employ the training sets of the held-in datasets for instruction tuning and their validation or test sets for held-in evaluation. For held-out evaluation, our aim is to understand how instruction tuning improves the model’s zero-shot performance on unseen data. We define two types of held-out data: 1) datasets not exposed to the model during training, but whose tasks are present in the held-in cluster; 2) datasets and their associated...
To avoid data contamination, datasets are selected carefully so that no evaluation data appear in

the held-in training cluster across different datasets. During instruction tuning, we mix all the held-in training sets and sample instruction templates uniformly for each dataset. The models are trained with the standard language modeling loss to directly generate the response given the instruction. Furthermore, for datasets that involve scene texts, we add OCR tokens in the instruction as supplementary information.
2.3 Instruction-aware Visual Feature Extraction

Existing zero-shot image-to-text generation methods, including BLIP-2, take an instruction-agnostic approach when extracting visual features. That results in a set of static visual representations being fed into the LLM, regardless of the task. In contrast, an instruction-aware vision model can adapt to the task instruction and produce visual representations most conducive to the task at hand. This is clearly advantageous if we expect the task instructions to vary considerably for the same input image. We show the architecture of InstructBLIP in Figure 3. 2.4 Balancing Training Datasets
Due to the large number of training datasets and the significant differences in the size of each dataset,
mixing them uniformly could cause the model to overfit smaller datasets and underfit larger datasets.

To mitigate the problem, we propose to sample datasets with probabilities proportional to the square root of their sizes, or the numbers of training samples. Generally, given D datasets with sizes {S1, S2, . . . , SD}, the probability of a data sample being selected from a dataset d during training
is pd =

√SdPD i=1 √Si . On top of this formula, we make manual adjustments to the weights of certain datasets to improve optimization. This is warranted by inherent differences in the datasets and tasks that require varying levels of training intensity despite similar sizes. To be specific, we lower the weight of A-OKVQA, which features multiple-choice questions, and increase the weight of OKVQA, which requires open-ended text generation. In Table 2, we show that the balanced dataset sampling strategy improves overall performance for both held-in evaluation and held-out generalization.
2.5 Inference Methods

During inference time, we adopt two slightly different generation approaches for evaluation on different datasets. For the majority of datasets, such as image captioning and open-ended VQA, the instruction-tuned model is directly prompted to generate responses, which are subsequently compared to the ground truth to calculate metrics. On the other hand, for classification and multi-choice VQA tasks, we employ a vocabulary ranking method following previous works [46, 22, 21]. Specifically, we still prompt the model to generate answers, but restrict its vocabulary to a list of candidates. Then,
we calculate log-likelihood for each candidate and select the one with the highest value as the final
prediction. This ranking method is applied to ScienceQA, IconQA, A-OKVQA (multiple-choice),
HatefulMemes, Visual Dialog, MSVD, and MSRVTT datasets. Furthermore, for binary classification,

5 Conclusion

In this paper, we present InstructBLIP, a simple yet novel instruction tuning framework towards gen- eralized vision-language models. We perform a comprehensive study on vision-language instruction tuning and demonstrate the capability of InstructBLIP models to generalize to a wide range of unseen tasks with state-of-the-art performance. Qualitative examples also exhibit InstructBLIP’s various 9

capabilities on instruction following, such as complex visual reasoning, knowledge-grounded image description, and multi-turn conversations. Furthermore, we show that InstructBLIP can serve as an enhanced model initialization for downstream task finetuning, achieving state-of-the-art results. We hope that InstructBLIP can spur new research in general-purpose multimodal AI and its applications.
